where: Section 1, paragraph after the four laws
problem: The blanket claim 'except there is no inverse. You cannot divide by a signal to undo convolution' is false as stated. Many signals do have a convolutional inverse (the inverse system, h * h_inv = δ), which is exactly what deconvolution and inverse filters use; only some signals lack one. A student reads this and concludes convolution can never be undone.
fix: Say: 'unlike ordinary multiplication, not every signal has an inverse. When an inverse exists it satisfies h(t)*h_inv(t)=δ(t), and the cascade of a system with its inverse is the identity system. There is no general rule for dividing one signal by another.'

problem: The convolution integral is written y(t)=∫ x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ with no limits, so the reader cannot tell it is taken over the whole real line, which matters for the proof hints that follow.
fix: Write y(t)=∫_{−∞}^{∞} x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ and say the integral runs over all τ.

problem: 'δ(t) has unit area and zero width' describes the impulse as if it were a pulse of vanishing width; δ is defined by its sifting property (unit area), not by a width.
fix: Say: 'δ(t) is defined by its unit area and sifting property, not by any graph or width.'
